description: Spec Section 27. Common objections with reframe patterns. Product-specific objections layer on top.

price.surface: It costs too much for what I might get from it.
price.reframe_pattern: Compare the one-time cost against the cost-of-inaction across a realistic use window.

quality.surface: I don't know if it will actually hold up.
quality.reframe_pattern: Show verifiable specs, warranty, and design decisions that back the claim.

trust.surface: I don't know this brand well enough.
trust.reframe_pattern: Show the company's process, philosophy, or verified customer language without inventing testimonials.

compatibility.surface: I'm not sure it works with my devices/situation.
compatibility.reframe_pattern: Trace the spec (wattage, ports, capacity) to the specific device or scenario.

complexity.surface: This looks complicated to set up or use.
complexity.reframe_pattern: Show a simple three-step (or fewer) real use flow.

necessity.surface: I probably don't really need this.
necessity.reframe_pattern: Anchor to a specific scenario the customer already recognizes; do not manufacture fear.

effectiveness.surface: How do I know it will actually deliver the result?
effectiveness.reframe_pattern: Trace feature -> mechanism -> benefit -> outcome with evidence at each step.

durability.surface: Will this last long enough to be worth it?
durability.reframe_pattern: Show design specs and warranty; avoid superlatives.

shipping_and_returns.surface: What if it doesn't work out?
shipping_and_returns.reframe_pattern: Show the actual return/warranty terms plainly.

timing.surface: This isn't the right time for me to invest.
timing.reframe_pattern: Anchor to preparedness timing (before, not during, the event) without manufactured urgency.
